disease_label_per_paper: Relapsing polychondritis presenting as fever of unknown origin with airway involvement and lymph node enlargement
presentation_summary: 54-year-old man had 3 months of moderate-to-high fever 38.5-39.4 C with mild headache and dry cough, without initial hoarseness, stridor, arthralgia, or dyspnea.
Admission labs showed ESR 63 mm/hr, hemoglobin 11.1 g/dL, albumin 38.5 g/L, platelets 391 x 10^9/L, procalcitonin 0.24 ng/mL, CRP 10.7 mg/dL, IL-6 44.12 pg/mL, and normal WBC count.
Broad infectious, autoimmune, malignancy, blood, sputum, BAL, bone marrow, and lymph node workup did not identify infection or lymphoma; lymph node biopsies showed nonspecific inflammation.
Chest CT evolved from cervical/supraclavicular/hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy to thickening of tracheal wall, airway wall thickening, lumen stenosis, and deformity.
Bronchoscopy showed obvious luminal stenosis with swollen thick pale mucosa and loss of cricoid cartilage; PET/CT showed symmetric FDG uptake in larynx, tracheobronchial tree, and lymph nodes.

Methylprednisolone 40 mg daily rapidly improved fever and cough; four-month follow-up showed no fever/lymph node relapse, but three-month CT showed progression of airway wall thickening and luminal stenosis.

actual_outcome: Fever and cough improved rapidly after methylprednisolone.
No relapse of fever or lymph node enlargement during 4-month follow-up.
Repeat CT at 3 months showed no hilar/mediastinal lymph node enlargement but progression of airway wall thickening and luminal stenosis.
